AUTHORIZING THE ALIEN PROPERTY CUSTODIAN
TO SELL CERTAIN PROPERTY AT PRIVATE SALE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by an Act of Congress entitled "An
act to define, regulate, and punish trading with the enemy and for other purposes",
approved October 6, 1917, known as the "Trading with the Enemy Act", and the
amendment to such act embodied in "An act making appropriations to supply
urgent deficiencies in the appropriations for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1918,
and prior fiscal years on account of war expenses and for other purposes", approved
March 28, 1918, and the amendment to such act embodied in "An act making
appropriations to supply deficiencies in appropriations for the fiscal year 'ending
June 30, 1919, and prior fiscal years on account of war expenses, and for other pur-
poses", approved November 4, 1918, to make certain orders such as that herein
contained, I hereby, in the public interest, make the following determination, order,
rule and regulation:
The Alien Property Custodian is hereby authorized to sell at private sale, at
such time and place as oim or to his authorized agent may seem advisable,
without public or other advertisement, for and in consideration of the sum of
SIXTY-FIvE HUNDRED ($6500) DOLLARS, certain real estate now being held and
administered by him as such Alien Property Custodian, and heretofore, upon re-
quirement, conveyed, transferred, assigned and delivered to him as the property of
J. Dietrich Luehrs and

provements thereon known by the street number as 291 19th Street.
My reasons for the foregoing determination, order, rule and regulation are:
(a) An advantageous offer for the sale of said real estate has been received by
the Alien Property Custodian, as shown by the appraisals of the property sold;
(b) An attempted sale at public auction would be a useless formality and
would involve unnecessary expenses, delay and inconvenience as the sum received
by this sale in excess of all appraisals is in excess of the value as indicated by
appraisals;
(c) It appears that it is to the interest of the trust held, in that its value will
be conserved by this sale by the substitution of the proceeds in lieu of the property
sold, because of the difficulty of the administration of such real estate and its con-
sequent deterioration;
(d) The character of this property is such that there are greater possibilities
of a decrease in its value than an increase, and that such sale made at this time
would, therefore, be to the best advantage of the trust.

By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States of
America, and pursuant to the provisions of Section 9 of the Act of Congress approved
on June 7, 1924, entitled, "An Act To provide for the protection of forest lands,
for the reforestation of denuded areas, for the extension of National Forests, and
for other purposes, in order to promote the continuous production of timber on
lands chiefly suitable therefor," the following described lands which comprise a
part of the Savanna Proving Ground Military Reservation in the State of Illinois,
and which, in the opinion of the Secretary of War and the Secretary of Agriculure,
are suitable for the production of timber, hereby are established as a National
Forest, to wit:
All of that part of the Savanna Proving Ground Military Reservation as
shown upon the map hereto attached and made a part hereof.
The National Forest hereby created shall be known as the Savanna National
Forest.
The said Savanna National Forest shall be administered by the Secretary of
Agriculture under such rules and regulations and in accordance with such general
plans as may be jointly approved by the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary
of War, for the use, occupation and protection of such lands and for the sale of
products therefrom.

At the request of the Attorney General, and with the consent of the Director
of the United States Veterans' Bureau and the Secretary of War, there is hereby
transferred back -to the War Department all that portion of the United States
Military Reservation known as Camp Sherman, together with all improvements
thereon, in the State of Ohio, assigned to the United States Veterans' Bureau by
Executive Order ##3558, dated October 11, 1921, for use in carrying out the provi-
sions of the Act of Congress approved August 9, 1921, (42 Stat. 147-150), excepting:
(1) The area transferred back to the War Department by Executive' Order
$#3633, dated February 7, 1922;
(2) The so-called "Mound City Group", returned to the custody and control
of the War Department by Executive Proclamation ##1653, dated
March 2, 1923, declaring said group to be a national monument site;
and
(3) That part of Camp Sherman north of a line beginning at a point on East
Liverpool Street at the Scioto River and running west on East Liverpool
Street to Columbus Avenue; thence south on Columbus Avenue to
Moundsville Street; then west on Moundsville Street to the junction
point of Frankfort and Egypt Pikes; then following along Egypt Pike
to the junction of Egypt Pike and Sandusky Boulevard; then due west
to the boundary line of the Government Reservation, as will appear on
a map of Camp Sherman, United States Army Cantonment, Chilli-
cothe, Ohio, known as the Building Location Plan, dated January, 191

site;
and
(3) That part of Camp Sherman north of a line beginning at a point on East
Liverpool Street at the Scioto River and running west on East Liverpool
Street to Columbus Avenue; thence south on Columbus Avenue to
Moundsville Street; then west on Moundsville Street to the junction
point of Frankfort and Egypt Pikes; then following along Egypt Pike
to the junction of Egypt Pike and Sandusky Boulevard; then due west
to the boundary line of the Government Reservation, as will appear on
a map of Camp Sherman, United States Army Cantonment, Chilli-
cothe, Ohio, known as the Building Location Plan, dated January, 1919.
This order is issued to enable the War Department to grant a revocable license
to the Department of Justice covering all that part of Camp Sherman, together
with all improvements thereon, lying south of the above line and including approxi-
mately six hundred and twenty acres east of the Scioto River known as the Rifle
Range, for use. for jail or penitentiary purposes as in the opinion of the Attorney
General may be needed.
CALVIN COOLIDGE
THE WHITE HOUSE,
August 14, 1925.
